title: Preserve custom launchers when installing mise wrappers
head: 36e3372357ef
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Application refresh reports success even if a wrapper installation failed
leads.consequence: Refreshing applications invokes the mise list with plain bash, and neither this caller nor mise.sh propagates intermediate nonzero statuses. With an existing claude directory, the new installer refuses it, the list continues, and refresh returns 0; upgrade-to-quattro:2374-2375 gets no warning. Next refresh repeats the same failure. The single-command installer still fails as intended. Propagate failure from the list or collect errors and fail after processing all wrappers.
leads.triage: dropped: masked failure only for a directory at a wrapper path via omarchy-refresh-applications; unusual input, low value

leads.summary: Byte-identical launchers with different permissions are replaced without a backup
leads.consequence: cmp -s checks content only. A user who made the stock launcher non-executable/private (mode 0600) has it replaced by mode 0755 with no .bak file or notice, reversing their permission override. Retain original metadata when equal or back up any file whose mode/other preserved attributes differ.
leads.triage: dropped: mode-only override also lost at base (rm then recreate), not a regression

leads.summary: A later wrapper migration rewrites a backup in the executable PATH directory
leads.consequence: The backup name is not hidden and matches the migration's $bin_dir/* glob. If an earlier generator's exact wrapper body is backed up, re-running the quiet-wrapper migration treats tool.bak.XXXXXX as another command, replaces its contents with a new launcher, moves the saved historical body into tool.bak.XXXXXX.bak.YYYYYY and prints another backup path. It can also happen after a partially failed migration left its marker pending. A user looking at the original announced backup path no longer gets its saved bytes; repeated scans expand copies. Exclude *.bak.* in migrations or keep backups outside the executable scan.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F2 (backup regenerated by 1787573629); no change

leads.summary: Backup copy does not preserve extended attributes on user launchers
leads.consequence: GNU cp -pP preserves mode, owner and timestamps, not xattrs. A user launcher with user.* metadata (or Linux capabilities stored in security.capability) is replaced, and the saved executable has no such metadata on restore; the new test checks bytes and 0700 only. If recoverability includes this metadata, preserve and assert xattrs (e.g. --preserve=all where supported), or explicitly limit the promise.
leads.triage: dropped: xattrs not preserved by cp -pP is a nitpick, low impact

leads.summary: Cleanly merging open #10168 fails the new preservation fixture
leads.consequence: #10168 adds @latest to an unversioned package. Its own mise-install-test passes with the merged generator, but this PR's new assertion demands mise use -g --quiet "tool" rather than "tool@latest"; it exits 1 at the first case, so the combined branch cannot pass test/shell. Make the new fixture check the intended package semantically or update its expected version after merging #10168.
leads.triage: factual, verified by coordinator (pr-10168.diff appends @latest; PR test line 21 greps exact "tool"; Sol merged run exit 1) and by Opus in self-check (plan6 part 1); published in Details Cross-PR

leads.summary: Other open wrapper changes require manual resolution at the staging/replacement hunk
leads.consequence: #13243 implements the same issue's alternative refusal-to-overwrite policy; merging it blindly with backup-and-replace is contradictory. Against each PR's own base/head, git merge-file flags conflicts with #13243 at the prewrite guard and cat, #13470 at rm/cat, #13677 at rm/cat, #13769 at rm/cat, #11514 at the generator's mise-use/cat body, and historical #9583 at its earlier generator form. These PRs are diverged rather than stacked; GitHub lists #13243, #13470, #13677 and #13769 as individually MERGEABLE against their base, while #11514 and #9583 are CONFLICTING. Rebase and retain the staged write and backup semantics while integrating desired wrapper body changes; do not simply restore rm -f and cat >launcher.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus related-PR conflicts (#13243, #13470, #13677, #13769); #11514 and #9583 conflicts noted privately, not published (outside the issue, low value)

leads.summary: Open #13781 introduces an additional bulk refresh that also replaces custom launchers
leads.consequence: If #13781 lands with this PR, its one-time restore-missing-stubs migration sources the full canonical installer even when a custom regular launcher exists at a stock name; the new installer moves it to .bak and makes the mise wrapper active. Unlike #13243 it does not leave the user's launcher in place. This is not a current-head migration; it is a conflict in behavior to settle when integrating #13781: only refresh truly missing paths if restore-missing is the goal.
leads.triage: dropped: #13781 interaction follows from this PR's intended backup-and-replace policy; not a defect of this PR

leads.summary: New symlink assertions do not verify the saved symlink's target
leads.consequence: The assertions only require that backup files are symlinks and that the original target was not modified. A realistic faulty backup that links to the launcher path instead of cloning the old symlink still passes every case, leaving both saved links pointing at the replacement launcher and making them unrecoverable. Check readlink of each backup against readlink of the original before invoking the installer.
leads.triage: factual, verified by reading test lines 29-38 and by Opus mutant (plan6 part 2); published as Optional test improvement

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Older wrappers Omarchy generated are also backed up, as executables on PATH that migration `1787573629` can turn into live wrappers.

### Older generated wrappers are backed up on every template refresh

The backup condition at `bin/omarchy-mise-install:72` compares only with the new template, so refreshing an older generated wrapper leaves a mode-755 `<name>.bak.XXXXXX` in `~/.local/bin` (on PATH), and nothing removes it. If `migrations/1787573629.sh` is still pending, its rescan regenerates that backup as a live wrapper `claude.bak.XXXXXX` and backs it up again. **Impact:** one update from before 2026-08-08 leaves two noise files per default wrapper, and with #13090 or #13614 merged, their migrations back up every current generated wrapper.

**Suggested change:** replace regular files matching the current template or the forms listed in `1787573629.sh` without a backup, and keep backups off PATH.

<details><summary>Reproducer: generated wrapper backup (fails at 36e33723)</summary>

Reproducer: refreshing a wrapper that omarchy-mise-install itself generated leaves an executable backup in ~/.local/bin

Save as `test/shell.d/mise-install-generated-backup-test.sh` and run `bash test/shell.d/mise-install-generated-backup-test.sh` from the repository root. It needs no mise (the wrapper is only written, never run).

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail
source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/base-test.sh"

test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT
export HOME="$test_tmp/home"
bin_dir="$HOME/.local/bin"
mkdir -p "$bin_dir"

# The wrapper omarchy-mise-install itself wrote before --quiet, i.e. the
# cooldown-export form that migrations/1787573629.sh regenerates.
printf '#!/bin/bash\nexport MISE_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE=0\nmise use -g "claude" || exit 1\nexec mise x "claude" -- "claude" "$@"\n' >"$bin_dir/claude"
chmod 755 "$bin_dir/claude"

"$ROOT/bin/omarchy-mise-install" claude

ls -l "$bin_dir" | awk 'NR > 1 { print $1, $NF }'
leftovers=$(find "$bin_dir" -name 'claude.bak.*' -print)
[[ -z $leftovers ]] ||
  fail "refreshing a wrapper omarchy-mise-install generated leaves no backup on PATH" "$leftovers"
pass "refreshing a wrapper omarchy-mise-install generated leaves no backup on PATH"
```

Actual output at the PR head (36e33723), exit status 1. Stdout:

```
Saved existing launcher to /tmp/tmp.UHZJ1U8JOu/home/.local/bin/claude.bak.AxYPtD
-rwxr-xr-x claude
-rwxr-xr-x claude.bak.AxYPtD
```

Stderr:

```
/tmp/tmp.UHZJ1U8JOu/home/.local/bin/claude.bak.AxYPtD
not ok - refreshing a wrapper omarchy-mise-install generated leaves no backup on PATH
```

Actual output at the merge base (28ceaae7), exit status 0, stdout (stderr empty):

```
-rwxr-xr-x claude
ok - refreshing a wrapper omarchy-mise-install generated leaves no backup on PATH
```

</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer: backup regenerated by migration 1787573629 (fails at 36e33723)</summary>

Reproducer: a saved backup is picked up by migration 1787573629 and regenerated as a live wrapper named `claude.bak.XXXXXX`, with a second backup of the backup

Save as `test/shell.d/mise-install-backup-rescan-test.sh` and run `bash test/shell.d/mise-install-backup-rescan-test.sh` from the repository root. It runs the repository's own `migrations/1787573629.sh` with `bin/` on PATH, as `omarchy-migrate` would; nothing runs mise.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail
source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/base-test.sh"

test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT
export HOME="$test_tmp/home"
bin_dir="$HOME/.local/bin"
mkdir -p "$bin_dir"

# A wrapper as omarchy-mise-install wrote it from 2026-07-27 until migration
# 1786183928 arrived. On such a machine one `omarchy update` runs 1786183928
# (omarchy-refresh-applications -> install/user/mise.sh rewrites the wrapper by
# name) and then 1787573629, which scans ~/.local/bin/* for this same form.
printf '#!/bin/bash\nmise use -g "claude" || exit 1\nexec mise x "claude" -- "claude" "$@"\n' >"$bin_dir/claude"
chmod 755 "$bin_dir/claude"

"$ROOT/bin/omarchy-mise-install" claude
PATH="$ROOT/bin:$PATH" bash -euo pipefail "$ROOT/migrations/1787573629.sh"

find "$bin_dir" -mindepth 1 -printf '%f\n' | sort
for backup in "$bin_dir"/claude.bak.*; do
  [[ -e $backup ]] || continue
  grep -q -- '--quiet' "$backup" &&
    fail "a saved launcher is not regenerated as a live wrapper by a later migration" "$backup: $(cat "$backup")"
done
pass "a saved launcher is not regenerated as a live wrapper by a later migration"
```

Actual output at the PR head (36e33723), exit status 1. Stdout:

```
Saved existing launcher to /tmp/tmp.y4AmbITvP4/home/.local/bin/claude.bak.qOofqL
Regenerate mise wrappers that still print mise's own output to stdout
Saved existing launcher to /tmp/tmp.y4AmbITvP4/home/.local/bin/claude.bak.qOofqL.bak.KWMU2u
claude
claude.bak.qOofqL
claude.bak.qOofqL.bak.KWMU2u
```

Stderr:

```
/tmp/tmp.y4AmbITvP4/home/.local/bin/claude.bak.qOofqL: #!/bin/bash
export MISE_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE=0
mise use -g --quiet "claude" || exit 1
exec mise x "claude" -- "claude" "$@"
not ok - a saved launcher is not regenerated as a live wrapper by a later migration
```

Actual output at the merge base (28ceaae7), exit status 0, stdout (stderr empty):

```
Regenerate mise wrappers that still print mise's own output to stdout
claude
ok - a saved launcher is not regenerated as a live wrapper by a later migration
```

The same happens through the real runner: `omarchy-migrate` with only 1786183928 and 1787573629 pending, on a home holding three wrappers in the form above plus one hand-written `codex`, ends with 7 `*.bak.*` entries at the head (the intended `codex.bak.*`, plus `claude`, `gh` and `omp` each as `<name>.bak.X` regenerated with `--quiet` and `<name>.bak.X.bak.Y` holding the old form) and 0 at the merge base, where `codex` is overwritten.

</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** (at 36e33723, synthetic HOME):
- A hand-written regular file, a symlink and a dangling symlink are saved verbatim with their mode before replacement; symlink targets are untouched.
- An identical reinstall creates no backup.
- A failed backup exits 1 with the original launcher intact and no staged file left behind.
- The new test passes at the head and fails at the merge base; mise-install, quiet-wrapper migration, migrate-wrapper, Hermes CLI, preinstalls and default-agent tests pass at the head and on a local merge with the tip of the base branch `quattro`.

**Optional notes:**
- **Optional test improvement:** `backups=("$launcher".bak.*)` without `shopt -s nullglob` has one element when no backup exists, so the "one backup is created" count cannot fail for zero (the next `cmp` assertion still catches it). Adding nullglob makes the count meaningful.
- **Optional test improvement:** the symlink cases never compare `readlink` of the backup with the original link target, and "symlink target is untouched" compares against the first section's backup. A mutant that saves links pointing elsewhere passes all new assertions; comparing `readlink` output closes that.
- New exit-1 paths (a directory at the launcher path, an unreadable file, an unwritable `~/.local/bin` holding a writable launcher) now stop migrations that call `omarchy-mise-install` directly and the provisioning run of `install/user/mise.sh`, where the base exited 0. These are unusual inputs and the refusal is clearer, but the stale comment "Checked before anything is removed or written" (lines 17-22) and the short reflowed line there could be updated.

**Cross-PR:** a clean merge with #10168 fails the new test at `grep -Fq 'mise use -g --quiet "tool"'`, because #10168 writes `"tool@latest"`. #13470, #13677 and #13769 conflict textually in `bin/omarchy-mise-install`.

</details>

<details><summary>Other open PRs for this issue</summary>

- #13243: refuses (exit 1) to replace an unrecognised regular file instead of backing it up, so the user's launcher stays active, but a migration that installs over such a file directly fails, and it and every later migration stay pending; it recognises generated wrappers by a single-line grep and conflicts textually with this PR.

</details>
